papers.title: 5D Runge-Lenz Vector from Symplectic Reduction of 8D Harmonic Oscillator
papers.abstract: We derive the Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem from the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator through symplectic reduction. By rewriting the moment maps of the harmonic oscillator in terms of five-dimensional gamma matrices and the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators associated with the symplectic reduction, we identify the moment map expected to yield the Runge-Lenz vector. We then perform the reduction with respect to the SU(2) symmetry, derive the five-dimensional Kepler Hamiltonian, and show explicitly that the identified moment map reduces to the Runge-Lenz vector.

papers.title: Design and Characterization of High Efficiency Single-stage Electromagnetic Coil Guns
papers.abstract: This study presents several novel approaches to improve the efficiency of a single-stage coil gun. Conventional designs typically feature a uniformly wound solenoid and a ferrite projectile. For our research, we constructed a microcontroller-based prototype to test several new enhancements, including the use of a bipolar current pulse, a stepped multilayer coil with non-uniform winding densities, and the replacement of conventional ferrite projectiles with a neodymium permanent magnet. These modifications were designed to reduce energy loss and improve projectile acceleration by changing magnetic field strength and effectively controlling the magnetic flux. The experimental results show that the proposed methods resulted in significant efficiency improvements, with the varying current pulse and stepped coil design providing enhanced magnetic force at key points in the projectile's path, and the permanent magnet projectile contributing to higher velocities and efficiencies by leveraging the current pulses. Our findings suggest that combining these enhancements significantly improves coil gun performance, achieving higher velocities and efficiencies. These findings can be applied to future coil gun developments, such as multi-stage coil gun systems.
